summary: Paul K. Nietupski specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University and held a post at John Carroll University (attested 2008).
Paul Kingsbury works in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under the supervision of George Cardona (attested 2002).

Paul Kiparsky (born 1941) is a linguist and Indologist. He studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and under Morris Halle at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1962–1965), later holding a post at Stanford University (~1984).

Paul L. Swanson (born 1951) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Otani University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, attested 1985) under Minoru Kiyota, Kosai Fukushima, and Noriaki Hakamaya, later serving as professor at Nanzan University (attested 1991–2009).

Paul Mendes-Flohr (1941–2024) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Brooklyn College and Brandeis University. He held posts at Freie Universität Berlin, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (Director 1999–2006), and the University of Chicago (~1999–2024).

Paul Mus (1902–1969) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. Educated at EPHE, INALCO, Oxford, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi and others, he held posts at EFEO (1927–1940), EPHE, Collège de France (1946–1969), and Yale (1951).
Paul Passy (1859–1940) was a linguist who studied under Ferdinand de Saussure. He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from ~1889 to 1913.

Paul Pelliot (1878–1945) worked in Sinology, Central Asian studies, and Tibetology, studying at INALCO, the Sorbonne, and Sciences Po under Édouard Chavannes and Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at EFEO (1900) and Collège de France (1909; chair 1911–1945).

Paul R. Brass (1936–2022) specialized in Indology and political science. Educated at Harvard College, the University of Chicago (~1958–1960), and Harvard University (~1958–1964), he spent his career at the University of Washington (~1967–2001).
Paul Regnaud (1838–1910) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the University of Lyon from ~1879 to 1908.

Paul Ricœur (1913–2005) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Rennes and Paris. He held posts at Strasbourg, Paris Nanterre, Université catholique de Louvain, and the University of Chicago (1970–1985).

Paul Tedesco (1898–1980) was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied at the University of Vienna (1916–1921). He held research posts at Princeton and was an associate and full professor at Yale University (1943–1966).

Paul Thieme (1905–2001) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Göttingen and Berlin under Hermann, Sieg, Andreas, Schulze, and Lüders, he held posts at Allahabad, Breslau, Halle-Wittenberg (1941–1953), Frankfurt, Yale (1954–1960), and Tübingen (1960–1973).

Paul Tillich (1886–1965) was a philosopher and theologian educated at Berlin, Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, and Breslau. He held posts at Berlin, Marburg, TU Dresden, Leipzig, Frankfurt, Union Theological Seminary (1933–1955), Harvard (1955–1962), and Chicago (1962–1965).
Paul W. Kroll (born 1948) is a scholar of Sinology who studied at the University of Michigan (~1970–1976). He held posts at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 1986, ~1989–2019).

Paul Williams (born 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Sussex and Oxford (DPhil 1978), was Bowra Research Fellow at Wadham College, and served as Emeritus Professor of Indian and Tibetan Philosophy at the University of Bristol (~1980–2011).

Paul de Lagarde (1827–1891) was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. Educated at Berlin under Friedrich Rückert and at Halle-Wittenberg, he held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1851–1854) and Göttingen (~1869–1891).

Paula Arai specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Kalamazoo College, Waseda, and Harvard (PhD 1993) under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Wilfred Cantwell Smith, holding posts at Vanderbilt, LSU, Carleton, and the Institute of Buddhist Studies (2023).

Paulinus of St. Bartholomew (1748–1806) worked in Indology and linguistics. Educated at Charles University and in Rome, he served as a missionary in the Malabar Mission (1776–1789) and later held posts with the Congregation of the Index and Pontifical Urban University.
Pavankumar Satuluri works in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held academic posts at Chinmaya Vishwavidyapeeth and the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (attested 2024–2025).
